# ARCaptcha Consolidated Documentation Context

> This document contains the consolidated, complete technical documentation for ARCaptcha. It is optimized for ingestion by Large Language Models and AI coding assistants in a single request.

---

## 1. Overview & Security Architecture

ARCaptcha protects web and mobile applications against bots, automated scraping, credential stuffing, SMS fraud, and spam.

### Security Principles: Site Key vs. Secret Key
Every ARCaptcha integration relies on two distinct cryptographic keys obtained from the ARCaptcha dashboard (https://dashboard.arcaptcha.co):

1. **Site Key (`site_key`)**:
   - **Environment**: Client-side (Public).
   - **Usage**: Configured in HTML markup (`data-site-key="YOUR_SITE_KEY"`) or passed as a parameter in JavaScript `arcaptcha.render()` / SDK components.
   - **Security**: Publicly accessible in frontend code; identifies your site to ARCaptcha's widget service.

2. **Secret Key (`secret_key`)**:
   - **Environment**: Server-side (Private).
   - **Usage**: Used exclusively by your backend server to authenticate token verification requests to `https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify`.
   - **Security Rule**: NEVER expose the Secret Key in client-side code, mobile application bundles, repository commits, or public scripts. Always store it in server environment variables (e.g., `ARCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`).

---

## 2. Integration Flow

1. **Frontend Script Load**: The browser loads the ARCaptcha JavaScript SDK (`https://nwidget.arcaptcha.ir/1/api.js`).
2. **Widget Render**: The widget renders inside a container element with class `arcaptcha` and `data-site-key`.
3. **Challenge Completion**: The user completes the CAPTCHA challenge (interactive or invisible).
4. **Token Generation**: Upon successful challenge resolution, ARCaptcha injects a hidden form input with name `arcaptcha-token` containing the challenge token string.
5. **Form Submission**: The user submits the form. The client sends `arcaptcha-token` along with form data to the customer backend server.
6. **Server Verification**: The customer backend sends a POST request to `https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify` with `site_key`, `secret_key`, and `challenge_id` (the token).
7. **Decision**: The backend inspects the verification response `success` field (`true` or `false`) and allows or blocks the user action accordingly.

---

## 3. Client-Side Integration

### Standard HTML Form Integration

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>ARCaptcha Protected Form</title>
    <!-- Load ARCaptcha API Script -->
    <script src="https://nwidget.arcaptcha.ir/1/api.js" async defer></script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <form action="/login" method="POST">
      <input type="text" name="username" placeholder="Username" required />
      <input type="password" name="password" placeholder="Password" required />

      <!-- ARCaptcha Widget Container -->
      <div class="arcaptcha" data-site-key="YOUR_SITE_KEY"></div>

      <!-- The hidden input `arcaptcha-token` is automatically inserted after solve -->
      <button type="submit">Log In</button>
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```

### Mobile WebView Domain Setting
When embedding the widget within mobile WebViews, pass the domain parameter in the script tag:
```html
<script src="https://nwidget.arcaptcha.ir/1/api.js?domain=example.com" async defer></script>
```

---

## 4. Configuration & JavaScript API

### Container Attributes & Render Parameters

| Attribute | Render Option | Type / Values | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `data-site-key` | `site_key` | string | (Required) | Public site key. |
| `data-size` | `size` | `'normal'` \| `'invisible'` | `'normal'` | Size of the widget. |
| `data-theme` | `theme` | `'light'` \| `'dark'` | `'light'` | Color theme. |
| `data-color` | `color` | CSS color name or hex | - | Theme accent color. |
| `data-error-print` | `error_print` | `'0'` \| `'1'` | `'0'` | Enable (`0`) or disable (`1`) error messages below widget. |
| `data-lang` | `lang` | `'en'` \| `'fa'` | `'fa'` | Widget language. |
| `data-callback` | `callback` | function / string | - | Triggered upon successful solve. Passes `token`. |
| `data-rendered-callback` | `rendered_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered after widget rendering finishes. |
| `data-error-callback` | `error_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered upon error during challenge. |
| `data-reset-callback` | `reset_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when widget is reset. |
| `data-expired-callback` | `expired_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when challenge solution expires. |
| `data-chlexpired-callback` | `chlexpired_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when open challenge expires. |
| `data-blocked-callback` | `blocked_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when client is detected as bot. |
| `data-clicked-callback` | `clicked_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when checkbox clicked or `execute` invoked. |
| `data-opened-callback` | `opened_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when challenge modal opens. |
| `data-closed-callback` | `closed_callback` | function / string | - | Triggered when challenge modal closes. |

### Global JavaScript Methods (`window.arcaptcha`)

1. `arcaptcha.render(container, params)`:
   - Explicitly renders the widget inside `container` (DOM selector string or HTMLElement).
   - `params`: Object with configuration properties (`site_key`, `size`, `callback`, etc.).
   - Returns: Unique `widgetID`.

2. `arcaptcha.execute(widgetID)`:
   - Programmatically triggers the ARCaptcha challenge.
   - Typically used in invisible mode.
   - Returns a Promise resolving to `{ arcaptcha_token }` or rejecting on failure.

3. `arcaptcha.reset(widgetID)`:
   - Resets the specified widget (or default widget if omitted) so a new challenge can be solved.

4. `arcaptcha.getArcToken(widgetID)`:
   - Returns the current challenge token string for the specified widget.

---

## 5. Invisible Captcha

Invisible CAPTCHA operates without rendering a visible checkbox widget. The user interaction only presents a visual challenge when risk assessment requires human verification.

### Option A: Automatic Button Binding
Bind the challenge directly to a submit button:
```html
<form id="login-form" action="/login" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="username" required />
  <button
    class="arcaptcha"
    data-site-key="YOUR_SITE_KEY"
    data-callback="onSubmit"
  >
    Submit
  </button>
</form>

<script>
  function onSubmit(token) {
    // Hidden token input is already populated or token passed here
    document.getElementById("login-form").submit();
  }
</script>
```

### Option B: Programmatic Invisible Execution
```html
<script src="https://nwidget.arcaptcha.ir/1/api.js" async defer></script>
<script>
  let widgetId = null;

  function initCaptcha() {
    widgetId = arcaptcha.render("#captcha-box", {
      site_key: "YOUR_SITE_KEY",
      size: "invisible",
      callback: (token) => {
        document.getElementById("demo-form").submit();
      }
    });
  }

  function handleFormSubmit(event) {
    event.preventDefault();
    if (widgetId !== null) {
      arcaptcha.execute(widgetId);
    }
  }

  window.onload = initCaptcha;
</script>

<form id="demo-form" action="/submit" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="name" required />
  <div id="captcha-box"></div>
  <button onclick="handleFormSubmit(event)">Submit</button>
</form>
```

---

## 6. Server-Side Verification API

### Endpoint Specification
- **URL**: `https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify`
- **Method**: `POST`
- **Headers**: `Content-Type: application/json`

### Request Payload
```json
{
  "site_key": "YOUR_PUBLIC_SITE_KEY",
  "secret_key": "YOUR_PRIVATE_SECRET_KEY",
  "challenge_id": "TOKEN_FROM_ARCAPTCHA_TOKEN_POST_DATA"
}
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `site_key` | string | Yes | The site key associated with your domain. |
| `secret_key` | string | Yes | Your private account secret key. |
| `challenge_id` | string | Yes | The value of `arcaptcha-token` received from the client submission. |

### Response Schema
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "error-codes": []
}
```

### Error Codes Reference
- `missing-input-sitekey`: The `site_key` parameter is missing.
- `missing-input-secret`: The `secret_key` parameter is missing.
- `missing-input-response`: The `challenge_id` parameter is missing.
- `bad-request`: Malformed or invalid request body.
- `invalid-input-sitekey`: The `site_key` parameter is invalid or malformed.
- `invalid-input-secret`: The `secret_key` parameter is invalid or malformed.
- `invalid-input-response`: The `challenge_id` is invalid, expired, or malformed.
- `timeout-or-duplicate`: The challenge has expired or has already been verified.

## 8. Server Verification Code Implementations

### Node.js / TypeScript Example
```typescript
import axios from "axios";

interface VerifyResponse {
  success: boolean;
  "error-codes"?: string[];
}

export async function verifyArcaptcha(token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const url = "https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify";
  const siteKey = process.env.ARCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY!;
  const secretKey = process.env.ARCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY!;

  try {
    const response = await axios.post<VerifyResponse>(
      url,
      {
        site_key: siteKey,
        secret_key: secretKey,
        challenge_id: token,
      },
      {
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        timeout: 5000,
      }
    );
    return Boolean(response.data?.success);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("ARCaptcha verification network error:", error);
    return false;
  }
}
```

### Python Example
```python
import os
import requests

def verify_arcaptcha(token: str) -> bool:
    url = "https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify"
    payload = {
        "site_key": os.environ["ARCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY"],
        "secret_key": os.environ["ARCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY"],
        "challenge_id": token,
    }
    try:
        res = requests.post(
            url,
            json=payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            timeout=5,
        )
        data = res.json()
        return bool(data.get("success", False))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"ARCaptcha verification failed: {exc}")
        return False
```

### Go Example
```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"time"
)

type VerifyRequest struct {
	SiteKey     string `json:"site_key"`
	SecretKey   string `json:"secret_key"`
	ChallengeID string `json:"challenge_id"`
}

type VerifyResponse struct {
	Success    bool     `json:"success"`
	ErrorCodes []string `json:"error-codes,omitempty"`
}

func VerifyArcaptcha(token string) (bool, error) {
	client := &http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second}
	reqBody, err := json.Marshal(VerifyRequest{
		SiteKey:     os.Getenv("ARCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY"),
		SecretKey:   os.Getenv("ARCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY"),
		ChallengeID: token,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	resp, err := client.Post(
		"https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify",
		"application/json",
		bytes.NewBuffer(reqBody),
	)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	var result VerifyResponse
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&result); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	return result.Success, nil
}
```

### cURL Example
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.arcaptcha.co/arcaptcha/api/verify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "site_key": "YOUR_SITE_KEY",
    "secret_key": "YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
    "challenge_id": "TOKEN_FROM_FORM"
  }'
```

## 9. AI Agent Integration & Onboarding

### 1-Click Prompt
```text
Please read https://docs.arcaptcha.co/onboard.md and help me integrate ARCaptcha into this project.
```

### Supported AI Assistants
- **Claude Code**: Terminal invocation (`claude "..."`) and deep link `claude-cli://open?q=...`.
- **Cursor**: Composer / Chat prompt injection and deep link `https://cursor.com/link/prompt?text=...`.
- **ChatGPT**: Web & desktop session and deep link `https://chatgpt.com/?q=...`.
- **OpenCode**: CLI prompt input, automated clipboard copying, and deep link `opencode://open?prompt=...`.

### Security Principles
- Never expose `secret_key` in client-side code, git repositories, or frontend bundles.
- Keep `secret_key` in server environment variables (e.g. `ARCAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`).
- Provide only `site_key` for client-side HTML containers and widgets.
